entries.title: Judges 10:1
segments:
He dwelt in Shamir; after he became judge; as this was a more central part of the country, and a more convenient place for a judge than any in his own tribe. 
 
Good rulers are the gift of God, and are designed, through the enactment and execution of good laws, to be for the protection and defence of the people.

entries.title: Judges 10:3
segments: A Gileadite; he was the first judge from the east side of Jordan.

entries.title: Judges 10:6
segments: Though a course of sinning has often been tried, and always found to lead in the end to misery, yet such is the folly and wickedness of men, that they will try it again with as much eagerness and confidence of success, as if the experiment had never been made.

entries.title: Judges 10:7
segments: Philistines; they lived on the west of the Israelites, and the children of Ammon on the east.

entries.title: Judges 10:8
segments: That year; the oppression of both began about the same time.  That part of the Ammonites lasted eighteen years, and that of the Philistines forty.

entries.title: Judges 10:10
segments: Men who in prosperity cast off the fear of the Lord, and openly rebel against him, in adversity, and when suffering the effects of their sins, often feel their need of his help.

entries.title: Judges 10:12
segments: The Moabites; probably an Arabian tribe.

entries.title: Judges 10:13
segments: I will deliver you no more; he would not, unless they should repent of their sins.

entries.title: Judges 10:14
segments: Cry unto the gods; this was designed to make them feel more deeply the worthlessness of their idols, and their need of help from Jehovah.

entries.title: Judges 10:15
segments: Though God might justly leave men to the consequences of their transgressions and never again deliver them, yet when they feel and acknowledge his righteousness, and turn heartily to him, he has compassion on them and opens the way for their relief.

entries.title: Judges 10:17
segments:
In Gilead; on the east of Jordan. 
 
  Mizpeh; near mount Gilead.
